headline: FULA Network Reaches 24 Nodes as DePIN Storage Matures
subtitle: Functionland's quiet growth and sandboxed AI integration position it inside one of crypto's fastest-moving infrastructure categories.
briefing:
Functionland's FULA network has grown to 24 active nodes — up from 23 a week prior — a modest but consistent uptick that reflects the community-driven model at the project's core. <cite index="11-1,11-5">Functionland operates as a decentralized cloud alternative, prioritizing privacy and enabling users to own their data without ads or subscriptions.</cite> That positioning lands it squarely inside a sector gaining serious traction: <cite index="9-9">as of May 2026, CoinGecko tracks 265 DePIN tokens with a combined market cap of approximately $18.92 billion, with sector on-chain revenue from paying customers reaching roughly $150 million in January 2026 alone.</cite>

Functionland's most differentiated near-term move remains its FxFiles MCP integration, which allows AI assistants sandboxed, read-write-only access to individual user folders. The timing is apt: <cite index="21-2,21-3">in just 18 months since Anthropic open-sourced the Model Context Protocol, MCP has surpassed 97 million monthly SDK downloads and is now supported by every major AI vendor, including OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and AWS.</cite> By anchoring to this rapidly adopted standard, Functionland gives developers a familiar on-ramp to decentralized storage.

Looking to Q3, <cite index="14-7,14-8,14-9">Functionland's roadmap calls for releasing an open-source monetization plan that distributes revenue among storers, application developers, and content creators — a model the team estimates could deliver up to 13 times higher revenues compared with traditional cloud intermediaries.</cite> Whether that flywheel can attract enterprise data migration commitments will be the number to watch in the months ahead.
